## Question 1

In a first time, we will calculate the empirical variogramm.

```{r}
#| label: empirical variogramm
#| fig-height: 4

# Load required libraries
library(geoR)
library(gstat)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Data preparation and conversion to sf object
data(wolfcamp)
coords <- wolfcamp$coords
z      <- wolfcamp$data

# Combine into a data.frame and convert to sf (Cartesian coordinates, no CRS needed)
df_wolfcamp <- data.frame(x = coords[, 1], y = coords[, 2], z = z)
dataset_sf  <- st_as_sf(df_wolfcamp, coords = c("x", "y"))

# 2. Dynamic formula creation
# "~ 1" means we are studying the raw variable, without external trend
formule <- as.formula(paste("z", "~ 1"))

# 3. Calculation of the experimental variogram
# gstat automatically calculates distances and groups points into bins
vario_exp <- variogram(formule, data = dataset_sf)

# 4. Graph creation with ggplot2
ggplot(vario_exp, aes(x = dist, y = gamma)) +
  geom_point(color = "#2c3e50", size = 3) +
  geom_line(color = "#3498db", linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(
    title = "Variogram",
    subtitle = paste("Evolution of the spatial variance for :", "z (wolfcamp)"),
    x = "Distance",
    y = "Semi-variance (Gamma)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


```

Now, we will compare the empirical variogramm with the diverse variogramm models. First of all, we analyse the trend of the diverse covariance functions.

```{r}
#| label: covariance functions
#| fig-height: 4


# ==============================================================================
# Geostatistical covariance functions 
# ==============================================================================

# 1. Spherical Model
spherical_cov <- function(h, sigma2, phi) {
  # C(h) = sigma^2 * (1 - 3h/(2phi) + h^3/(2phi^3)) for 0 < h <= phi, 0 otherwise
  ifelse(h == 0, sigma2,
         ifelse(h <= phi, sigma2 * (1 - 1.5 * (h / phi) + 0.5 * (h / phi)^3), 0))
}

# 2. Powered Exponential Model
exponential_cov <- function(h, sigma2, phi, kappa = 1) {
  # C(h) = sigma^2 * exp(-|h/phi|^kappa)
  sigma2 * exp(-(h / phi)^kappa)
}

# 3. Rational Quadratic Model
rational_quadratic_cov <- function(h, sigma2, phi) {
  # C(h) = sigma^2 * (1 - h^2 / (phi^2 + h^2))
  sigma2 * (1 - (h^2) / (phi^2 + h^2))
}

# 4. Wave Model
wave_cov <- function(h, sigma2, phi) {
  # C(h) = sigma^2 * (sin(h/phi) / (h/phi))
  ifelse(h == 0, sigma2, sigma2 * sin(h / phi) / (h / phi))
}

# 5. Matern Model
matern_cov <- function(h, sigma2, phi, kappa) {
  # Uses the modified Bessel function of the second kind K_kappa
  ifelse(h == 0, sigma2,
         sigma2 * (1 / (2^(kappa - 1) * gamma(kappa))) * 
           (h / phi)^kappa * besselK(x = h / phi, nu = kappa))
}

# ==============================================================================
# Visualizations: Plotting the models with varying parameters
# ==============================================================================

# Setup plotting grid (2 rows, 3 columns)
par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

# Sequence of distances h
h_seq <- seq(0, 2, length.out = 300)
fixed_sigma2 <- 1 # Fix the variance (sill) to 1 to compare shapes

# -- Plot 1: Spherical (Varying phi) --
plot(h_seq, spherical_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.5), type = "l", col = "blue", 
     lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "Distance (h)", ylab = "C(h)", 
     main = "Spherical\n(Varying phi)")
lines(h_seq, spherical_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 1.0), col = "red", lwd = 2)
lines(h_seq, spherical_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 1.5), col = "green3", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("phi = 0.5", "phi = 1.0", "phi = 1.5"), 
       col = c("blue", "red", "green3"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")

# -- Plot 2: Exponential (Varying phi, with kappa=1) --
plot(h_seq, exponential_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.2), type = "l", col = "blue", 
     lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "Distance (h)", ylab = "C(h)", 
     main = "Exponential (kappa=1)\n(Varying phi)")
lines(h_seq, exponential_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.5), col = "red", lwd = 2)
lines(h_seq, exponential_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 1.0), col = "green3", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("phi = 0.2", "phi = 0.5", "phi = 1.0"), 
       col = c("blue", "red", "green3"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")

# -- Plot 3: Powered Exponential (Varying kappa, with phi=0.5) --
plot(h_seq, exponential_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.5, kappa = 0.5), type = "l", col = "blue", 
     lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "Distance (h)", ylab = "C(h)", 
     main = "Powered Exp. (phi=0.5)\n(Varying kappa)")
lines(h_seq, exponential_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.5, kappa = 1.0), col = "red", lwd = 2)
lines(h_seq, exponential_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.5, kappa = 2.0), col = "green3", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("kappa = 0.5", "kappa = 1.0", "kappa = 2.0"), 
       col = c("blue", "red", "green3"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")

# -- Plot 4: Rational Quadratic (Varying phi) --
plot(h_seq, rational_quadratic_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.2), type = "l", col = "blue", 
     lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "Distance (h)", ylab = "C(h)", 
     main = "Rational Quadratic\n(Varying phi)")
lines(h_seq, rational_quadratic_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.5), col = "red", lwd = 2)
lines(h_seq, rational_quadratic_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 1.0), col = "green3", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("phi = 0.2", "phi = 0.5", "phi = 1.0"), 
       col = c("blue", "red", "green3"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")

# -- Plot 5: Wave (Varying phi) --
plot(h_seq, wave_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.1), type = "l", col = "blue", 
     lwd = 2, ylim = c(-0.3, 1), xlab = "Distance (h)", ylab = "C(h)", 
     main = "Wave\n(Varying phi)")
lines(h_seq, wave_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.2), col = "red", lwd = 2)
lines(h_seq, wave_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.4), col = "green3", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("phi = 0.1", "phi = 0.2", "phi = 0.4"), 
       col = c("blue", "red", "green3"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray") # Zero line to better see the oscillation

# -- Plot 6: Matern (Varying kappa, as shown in slide 32) --
plot(h_seq, matern_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.25, kappa = 0.1), type = "l", col = "blue", 
     lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "Distance (h)", ylab = "C(h)", 
     main = "Matern (phi=0.25)\n(Varying kappa)")
lines(h_seq, matern_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.25, kappa = 0.5), col = "red", lwd = 2)
lines(h_seq, matern_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.25, kappa = 1.5), col = "green3", lwd = 2)
lines(h_seq, matern_cov(h_seq, fixed_sigma2, phi = 0.25, kappa = 2.0), col = "purple", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("kappa = 0.1", "kappa = 0.5", "kappa = 1.5", "kappa = 2.0"), 
       col = c("blue", "red", "green3", "purple"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")

# Reset plotting layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r}
# COMPLETE GEOSTATISTICAL FITTING ALGORITHM (WOLFCAMP DATASET)
# 1. Calculates the real empirical variogram using gstat
# 2. Fits the 5 theoretical models by minimizing the absolute error integral
# 3. Plots the empirical points vs the best theoretical curve for ALL 5 models
# ==============================================================================

# Load required libraries
library(geoR)
library(gstat)
library(sf)
library(MBA)
library(ggplot2)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1: LOAD DATA & CALCULATE THE REAL EMPIRICAL VARIOGRAM
# ==============================================================================

cat("1. Loading 'wolfcamp' data and calculating empirical variogram...\n")

# Load wolfcamp dataset
data(wolfcamp)
coords <- wolfcamp$coords
z      <- wolfcamp$data

# Combine coordinates and data into a standard data.frame
df_wolfcamp <- data.frame(
  x = coords[, 1],
  y = coords[, 2],
  z = z
)

# Convert to sf object (Cartesian grid, no specific EPSG needed)
dataset_sf <- st_as_sf(df_wolfcamp, coords = c("x", "y"))

# Calculate empirical variogram (assuming constant mean: z ~ 1)
formule <- as.formula("z ~ 1")
vario_exp <- variogram(formule, data = dataset_sf)

# Extract the empirical data needed for the fitting algorithm
empirical_data <- data.frame(h = vario_exp$dist, gamma = vario_exp$gamma)

# Print quick summary of empirical variogram to help adjust the grid later
cat(sprintf("   -> Empirical distance (h) range: [%.2f, %.2f]\n", 
            min(empirical_data$h), max(empirical_data$h)))
cat(sprintf("   -> Empirical semi-variance (gamma) range: [%.2f, %.2f]\n", 
            min(empirical_data$gamma), max(empirical_data$gamma)))

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: DEFINE THEORETICAL MODELS & GRIDS
# ==============================================================================

# Base covariance functions
spherical_cov <- function(h, sigma2, phi, ...) {
  ifelse(h == 0, sigma2,
         ifelse(h <= phi, sigma2 * (1 - 1.5 * (h / phi) + 0.5 * (h / phi)^3), 0))
}

powered_exponential_cov <- function(h, sigma2, phi, kappa, ...) {
  sigma2 * exp(-(h / phi)^kappa)
}

rational_quadratic_cov <- function(h, sigma2, phi, ...) {
  sigma2 * (1 - (h^2) / (phi^2 + h^2))
}

wave_cov <- function(h, sigma2, phi, ...) {
  ifelse(h == 0, sigma2, sigma2 * sin(h / phi) / (h / phi))
}

matern_cov <- function(h, sigma2, phi, kappa, ...) {
  ifelse(h == 0, sigma2,
         sigma2 * (1 / (2^(kappa - 1) * gamma(kappa))) * 
           (h / phi)^kappa * besselK(x = h / phi, nu = kappa))
}

# Wrapper function for semi-variogram WITH nugget
semi_variogram <- function(cov_func, h, sigma2, phi, nugget, ...) {
  ifelse(h == 0, 0, nugget + sigma2 - cov_func(h, sigma2, phi, ...))
}

# Define the parameter sequences (kept identical as requested)
sigma2_seq <- seq(20000, 40000, by = 500)  # 9 values
phi_seq    <- seq(1, 160, by = 10)    # 8 values
nugget_seq <- seq(1, 1000, by = 50)       # 21 values
kappa_seq  <- c(0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0)      # 5 values for kappa

# Grid for standard models: 9 * 8 * 21 = 1512 combinations
param_grid_base <- expand.grid(sigma2 = sigma2_seq, 
                               phi = phi_seq, 
                               nugget = nugget_seq)

# Grid for models with kappa: 1512 * 5 = 7560 combinations
param_grid_kappa <- expand.grid(sigma2 = sigma2_seq, 
                                phi = phi_seq, 
                                nugget = nugget_seq,
                                kappa = kappa_seq)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 3: EVALUATION FUNCTION (INTEGRAL ALGORITHM)
# ==============================================================================

find_best_model_integral <- function(cov_func, emp_data, grid, model_name) {
  
  continuous_emp_gamma <- approxfun(emp_data$h, emp_data$gamma, rule = 2)
  fine_h <- seq(min(emp_data$h), max(emp_data$h), length.out = 1000)
  dh <- diff(fine_h)[1] 
  
  fine_emp_values <- continuous_emp_gamma(fine_h)
  scores <- numeric(nrow(grid))
  has_kappa <- "kappa" %in% names(grid)
  
  for(i in 1:nrow(grid)) {
    params <- grid[i, ]
    
    if(has_kappa) {
      fine_theo_values <- semi_variogram(cov_func, fine_h, 
                                         sigma2 = params$sigma2, 
                                         phi = params$phi, 
                                         nugget = params$nugget,
                                         kappa = params$kappa)
    } else {
      fine_theo_values <- semi_variogram(cov_func, fine_h, 
                                         sigma2 = params$sigma2, 
                                         phi = params$phi, 
                                         nugget = params$nugget)
    }
    
    abs_diff <- abs(fine_emp_values - fine_theo_values)
    scores[i] <- sum((abs_diff[-1] + abs_diff[-length(abs_diff)]) / 2 * dh)
  }
  
  best_index <- which.min(scores)
  best_params <- grid[best_index, ]
  best_score <- scores[best_index]
  
  kappa_val <- ifelse(has_kappa, best_params$kappa, NA)
  
  return(list(model = model_name, 
              sigma2 = best_params$sigma2, 
              phi = best_params$phi, 
              nugget = best_params$nugget, 
              kappa = kappa_val,
              score = best_score))
}

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 4: EXECUTE OPTIMIZATION ON THE 5 THEORETICAL MODELS
# ==============================================================================

cat("\n2. Evaluating models against the real empirical variogram...\n")

res_spherical <- find_best_model_integral(spherical_cov, empirical_data, param_grid_base, "Spherical")
res_rational  <- find_best_model_integral(rational_quadratic_cov, empirical_data, param_grid_base, "Rational Quadratic")
res_wave      <- find_best_model_integral(wave_cov, empirical_data, param_grid_base, "Wave")

res_pow_exp   <- find_best_model_integral(powered_exponential_cov, empirical_data, param_grid_kappa, "Powered Exponential")
res_matern    <- find_best_model_integral(matern_cov, empirical_data, param_grid_kappa, "Matern")

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 5: FINAL SUMMARY
# ==============================================================================

results_summary <- data.frame(
  Model = c(res_spherical$model, res_pow_exp$model, res_rational$model, res_wave$model, res_matern$model),
  Score_Error = c(res_spherical$score, res_pow_exp$score, res_rational$score, res_wave$score, res_matern$score),
  Sigma2 = c(res_spherical$sigma2, res_pow_exp$sigma2, res_rational$sigma2, res_wave$sigma2, res_matern$sigma2),
  Phi = c(res_spherical$phi, res_pow_exp$phi, res_rational$phi, res_wave$phi, res_matern$phi),
  Nugget = c(res_spherical$nugget, res_pow_exp$nugget, res_rational$nugget, res_wave$nugget, res_matern$nugget),
  Kappa = c(res_spherical$kappa, res_pow_exp$kappa, res_rational$kappa, res_wave$kappa, res_matern$kappa)
)

# Sort by lowest error score
results_summary <- results_summary[order(results_summary$Score_Error), ]

cat("\n================ FINAL RESULTS ================\n")
print(results_summary, row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\n=> The absolute best fitting model is '%s' with an error score of %.2f\n", 
            results_summary$Model[1], results_summary$Score_Error[1]))

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 6: PLOT EMPIRICAL DATA VS ALL 5 BEST THEORETICAL MODELS
# ==============================================================================

cat("\n3. Generating final comparison plot for all 5 models...\n")

# Create a sequence of distances to draw smooth theoretical curves
h_theo <- seq(0, max(empirical_data$h) * 1.1, length.out = 500)

# Initialize an empty data frame to store all theoretical curves
all_theoretical_data <- data.frame()

# Loop through each model in the summary to generate its theoretical curve
for (i in 1:nrow(results_summary)) {
  m_name   <- results_summary$Model[i]
  m_sigma2 <- results_summary$Sigma2[i]
  m_phi    <- results_summary$Phi[i]
  m_nugget <- results_summary$Nugget[i]
  m_kappa  <- results_summary$Kappa[i]
  
  # Map model name to covariance function
  m_cov_func <- switch(m_name,
                       "Spherical" = spherical_cov,
                       "Powered Exponential" = powered_exponential_cov,
                       "Rational Quadratic" = rational_quadratic_cov,
                       "Wave" = wave_cov,
                       "Matern" = matern_cov)
  
  # Calculate theoretical gamma values
  if (is.na(m_kappa)) {
    gamma_theo <- semi_variogram(m_cov_func, h_theo, sigma2 = m_sigma2, phi = m_phi, nugget = m_nugget)
  } else {
    gamma_theo <- semi_variogram(m_cov_func, h_theo, sigma2 = m_sigma2, phi = m_phi, nugget = m_nugget, kappa = m_kappa)
  }
  
  # Append to the combined data frame
  temp_df <- data.frame(h = h_theo, gamma = gamma_theo, Model = m_name)
  all_theoretical_data <- rbind(all_theoretical_data, temp_df)
}

# Plot with ggplot2
final_plot_all <- ggplot() +
  # Empirical points (Black dots)
  geom_point(data = empirical_data, aes(x = h, y = gamma), color = "#2c3e50", size = 3, shape = 16) +
  # Theoretical smooth curves colored by model
  geom_line(data = all_theoretical_data, aes(x = h, y = gamma, color = Model), linewidth = 1) +
  # Labels and Title
  labs(
    title = "Empirical Variogram vs Best Fit for ALL 5 Models (Wolfcamp)",
    subtitle = "Comparison of the optimal parameter combinations for each theoretical model",
    x = "Distance (h)",
    y = "Semi-variance (Gamma)",
    color = "Theoretical Models"
  ) +
  # Use a nice color palette for the 5 lines
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  # Theme and styling
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(final_plot_all)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 7: PLOT EMPIRICAL DATA VS ONLY THE SINGLE BEST THEORETICAL MODEL
# ==============================================================================

cat("\n4. Generating plot for the SINGLE BEST theoretical model...\n")

# Extract the name and parameters of the absolute best model
best_model_name <- results_summary$Model[1]
best_sigma2     <- results_summary$Sigma2[1]
best_phi        <- results_summary$Phi[1]
best_nugget     <- results_summary$Nugget[1]
best_score      <- results_summary$Score_Error[1]

# Filter the theoretical data created in Step 6 for only the winning model
best_model_data <- subset(all_theoretical_data, Model == best_model_name)

# Create the dedicated plot
final_plot_best <- ggplot() +
  # Empirical points (Black dots)
  geom_point(data = empirical_data, aes(x = h, y = gamma), color = "#2c3e50", size = 3, shape = 16) +
  # Single best theoretical curve (Red line)
  geom_line(data = best_model_data, aes(x = h, y = gamma), color = "#e74c3c", linewidth = 1.2) +
  # Labels and dynamic title showing the exact parameters
  labs(
    title = sprintf("Empirical Variogram vs Best Fit: %s", best_model_name),
    subtitle = sprintf("Optimized parameters -> Nugget: %.0f | Sigma2: %.0f | Phi: %.0f | Error: %.2f", 
                       best_nugget, best_sigma2, best_phi, best_score),
    x = "Distance (h)",
    y = "Semi-variance (Gamma)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# Display the final single-model plot
print(final_plot_best)
```

## Question 2

```{r}
#| label: interpolation
#| fig-height: 4


# ==============================================================================
# LIKELIHOOD-BASED KRIGING (MLE / REML)
# Dataset: wolfcamp
# ==============================================================================

# Load required libraries
library(geoR)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load data (already in 'geodata' format expected by geoR)
data(wolfcamp)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. PARAMETER ESTIMATION VIA RESTRICTED MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD (REML)
# ==============================================================================

# Estimate the variogram parameters directly from the data.
# - trend = "1st": models X*beta with a linear spatial trend (z ~ x + y)
# - ini = c(2000, 50): initial values for optimization (sigma2, phi)
# - nug = 500: initial value for the nugget effect (tau^2)
# - lik.method = "REML": Restricted Maximum Likelihood (preferred over standard MLE)

cat("Estimating spatial parameters via REML...\n")
modele_reml <- likfit(wolfcamp, 
                      trend = "1st", 
                      ini = c(2000, 50), 
                      nug = 500, 
                      lik.method = "REML")

# Display optimal parameters found by likelihood estimation
print(modele_reml)

# ==============================================================================
# 3. CREATING THE PREDICTION GRID
# ==============================================================================

# Create a regular grid covering the spatial extent of wolfcamp coordinates
x_seq <- seq(min(wolfcamp$coords[,1]), max(wolfcamp$coords[,1]), length.out = 100)
y_seq <- seq(min(wolfcamp$coords[,2]), max(wolfcamp$coords[,2]), length.out = 100)
grille_prediction <- expand.grid(x = x_seq, y = y_seq)

# ==============================================================================
# 4. SPATIAL PREDICTION: CONDITIONAL EXPECTATION (KRIGING)
# ==============================================================================

# Use the estimated parameters (modele_reml) to compute the conditional 
# expectation (prediction) and kriging variance on the grid.
cat("\nComputing conditional expectation (Kriging) over the grid...\n")
krigeage_result <- krige.conv(wolfcamp, 
                              loc = grille_prediction, 
                              krige = krige.control(obj.model = modele_reml, trend.d = "1st", trend.l = "1st"))

# ==============================================================================
# 5. VISUALIZATION WITH GGPLOT2
# ==============================================================================

# Prepare data for ggplot
df_plot <- data.frame(
  x = grille_prediction$x,
  y = grille_prediction$y,
  Prediction = krigeage_result$predict,
  Variance = krigeage_result$krige.var
)

df_coords <- data.frame(x = wolfcamp$coords[,1], y = wolfcamp$coords[,2])

# Plot the interpolated surface
plot_prediction <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = df_plot, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = Prediction)) +
  geom_point(data = df_coords, aes(x = x, y = y), color = "black", size = 1.5, shape = 21, fill = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "Piezometric\nlevel") +
  labs(
    title = "Universal Kriging (REML Model)",
    subtitle = "Spatial interpolation with 1st order trend (z ~ x + y)",
    x = "X Coordinate",
    y = "Y Coordinate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

print(plot_prediction)

# Note: You can create a similar plot to visualize df_plot$Variance (uncertainty)

```
